gen-gf-paprika-gf-victor-mono: Paprika shouts across the page with big, scattered letters. Victor Mono, the monospace below, leaves its bowls open on one side and spaces its glyphs loosely, so paragraphs read like tidy, unhurried code.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-viga: Commanding in its scattered, wide-set letters, Paprika puts lowercase forms that fill the line right at the top of the page. Viga's plain sans strokes stay smooth.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-voces: Voces reads tall and crisp, its stems and hairlines nearly matching in thickness, which lets text move along without fuss. Under Paprika's loud heading, that plain sans restraint is the draw.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-winky-rough: Loud, loose and loaded with attitude. Paprika's lowercase fills the line like capitals, while Winky Rough sits close to cap height, and a modest body size would keep the two from competing.
gen-gf-paprika-gf-winky-sans: Paprika's lowercase swells to fill the line like capitals, with counters open like a reed sliced lengthwise. Winky Sans, a plain sans with capitals barely above lowercase, reads smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
gen-gf-paprika-outfit: Outfit draws its curves like bent cable, stopping well before they close, with no swelling or thinning anywhere along the stroke. Against Paprika's commanding heading, that wire-like simplicity is the pair's strength.
gen-gf-paprika-plus-jakarta-sans: Expressive is the right word for Paprika, whose lowercase forms fill the line like capitals and whose counters open wide. Plus Jakarta Sans answers with monoline sans text, curve endings held well apart.
gen-gf-paprika-sora: Big, loud and scattered. Paprika's lowercase fills the line, while Sora's plain sans has no swell at curve corners and keeps its c and s widely parted, a marker-drawn plainness that is the pair's strength.
gen-gf-phudu-clash-grotesk: Phudu draws open-ended curves with a ballpoint's pressure-free line, and Clash Grotesk, a sans-serif, carries on without any thick-and-thin modulation. That shared flat line weight is what holds the pair together.
gen-gf-phudu-fs-alpino: Phudu is bold and distinctive, with generous terminal openings on every curve in a ballpoint's pressure-free line. Alpino is a cozy, casual sans whose tall body makes ascenders look short beneath it.
